Definition: properly, a bubbling up, i.e. of water, a wave; of earth, mire or clay (cement); also a heap; hence, a chomer or dry measure
BiblicalUsage: Chomer is mortar and clay and a measure, the stuff of building and of weighing, and it carries three senses in one word. The builders of Babel use slime for mortar, Pharaoh makes Israel's lives bitter with bondage in mortar and brick, and Ezekiel fixes the homer as the measure of grain and oil.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mortar of Babel and the mortar of Egypt are the same word, because man's building and man's bondage are built of the same stuff. I hold that God measures what men build, and His measure is the one that stands.
